title: A tested resolution of the black-hole information paradox

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a precise, independently validated account of what happens to quantum information when a black hole evaporates. It would establish whether evaporation preserves information through unitary quantum evolution or instead produces a specific, demonstrable departure from unitarity. The paradox arises because semiclassical gravity predicts thermal radiation and mass loss, while extrapolating the usual information-loss account through complete evaporation appears to turn a pure quantum state into a mixed state.

A resolution must explain information behavior beyond reproducing an entropy curve. The Page curve describes how the radiation's entanglement entropy evolves: information-preserving evaporation requires the late radiation to carry correlations that change the entropy evolution expected from a straightforward thermal description. Holographic calculations have made substantial progress on this problem, including explanations of interior encoding and reconstruction. Reproducing the Page curve alone, however, does not establish full unitary evolution of the quantum state.

Proposed scope: the defining advance would combine an explicit evaporation mechanism, a derivation of its entropy evolution, and a discriminating check independent of the calculation producing that curve. Independent mathematical validation and empirical confirmation would establish different things. A consistency result could strengthen a conceptual resolution; a physical observation would be required to claim empirical confirmation of its account of black-hole evaporation.

significance.text: An independently validated resolution would establish how information behaves in black-hole evaporation and impose a major consistency requirement on theories describing that regime. If information is preserved, the theory must explain how the apparent information loss of the semiclassical description is avoided. If unitarity fails, the departure must be specified and demonstrated. Either outcome would address a central conflict at the intersection of quantum mechanics and gravity.

The holographic setting makes the consistency issue particularly sharp: the boundary conformal field theory evolves unitarily, requiring its gravitational description to preserve information. Understanding how the bulk description realizes that requirement could clarify the relationship between spacetime geometry, entanglement, and information recovery. Extending such an account to physically relevant evaporation would require establishing which conclusions survive beyond the assumptions and boundary conditions of the model.

Scope synthesis: settling this paradox would constrain the relationship between gravity and quantum mechanics in evaporation, without determining their entire relationship. It would not by itself provide a laboratory witness that gravity is non-classical, a complete ultraviolet theory, traversable wormholes, or practical energy extraction. Broader theoretical insights could follow, but each additional scientific or technological consequence would require its own argument and evidence.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is an account of evaporation precise enough to distinguish information preservation from a specified failure of unitarity, explain the relevant quantum-state evolution, and face a check that can discriminate between competing accounts. An entropy curve is an important constraint, but it does not by itself establish the complete information mechanism or prove full unitary evolution. The supplied evidence supports substantial progress within holographic frameworks without establishing an independently tested account for real black holes.

A concrete theoretical barrier is understanding the assumptions and scope of reconstruction. Penington's calculation uses the Ryu–Takayanagi formula and entanglement wedge reconstruction, both holographic ingredients. Tiny, non-perturbative reconstruction errors play a crucial role. Immediately after the Page time, reconstructing interior operators from the radiation requires knowledge of the initial black-hole state; reconstruction over larger classes of states becomes possible later. This initial-state restriction applies to the specified reconstruction task and time, rather than to every aspect of the Page-curve derivation.

A separate observational barrier is the extremely weak Hawking radiation expected from astrophysical black holes. The supplied 2025 survey attributes the lack of experimental verification to this minuscule radiation. Demonstrating information behavior would require a discriminating physical consequence, beyond establishing thermal emission or reproducing a mode-mixing relation. The supplied sources identify no decisive observable for that purpose, so the feasibility of a direct test remains uncertain.

current_state.text: Geoffrey Penington's “Entanglement Wedge Reconstruction and the Information Paradox” was first submitted on 20 May 2019, revised on 29 August 2020, and published as JHEP 09 (2020) 002. It studies an evaporating black hole in AdS/CFT with absorbing boundary conditions. The calculation finds a transition in the quantum Ryu–Takayanagi surface at the Page time and derives a Page curve. These are theoretical results within the specified holographic setting, rather than measurements of astrophysical Hawking radiation.

The calculation also describes part of the interior as encoded in early radiation. Directly after the Page time, interior operators can be reconstructed from the radiation only when the initial black-hole state is known; later reconstructions can cover larger classes of states. Non-perturbative reconstruction errors are essential to the account. Penington presents a resolution of information-paradox and firewall questions within AdS/CFT, so the achievement should not be reduced to merely drawing an entropy curve. Its model-specific explanatory success and its applicability to real evaporating black holes remain distinct questions.

Ricardo Bulcão Valente Ferrari and Samuel Bueno Soltau's “Black Hole Thermodynamics: Established Results, Unresolved Paradoxes, and Speculative Resolutions” was submitted on 4 July 2025 and revised on 10 December 2025. The supplied record identifies it as an arXiv survey and contains no journal version. Its authors describe persistent information-paradox challenges, discuss islands and replica wormholes as proposals suggesting preservation of unitarity, and report a lack of experimental verification. They also distinguish reproducing the Page curve from proving full unitary evolution. These are the survey authors' assessments, rather than evidence of universal agreement across the field.

Evidence coverage limits the breadth of this account. The supplied review used Penington's abstract and a PDF extraction that ends during page 37; the retained primary-paper text is therefore partial. The survey extraction includes all 11 pages through its references. Although the source artifacts were retrieved on 1 November 2026, the supplied search record is empty. These materials establish the dated theoretical achievements and the survey's December 2025 assessment, but do not establish a comprehensive account of all relevant literature or measurements through 1 November 2026. That coverage gap does not invalidate the supported calculations or demonstrate that later results do not exist.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed theoretical demonstration: publish a framework that explicitly states whether evaporation preserves information, derives the late-time entropy from its own rules, and explains the associated quantum-state evolution or specific failure of unitarity. Its assumptions, boundary conditions, reconstruction requirements, and treatment of non-perturbative effects should be explicit enough for independent researchers to reproduce the argument and identify where it could fail. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, not established community standards.
completion_criteria.label: Framework derives late-time entropy and specifies evaporation's information fate

completion_criteria.text: Proposed independent validation: require a discriminating check beyond the calculation that generated the Page curve. An independently established consistency requirement that competing accounts fail could provide conceptual validation. Empirical validation would instead require a predicted physical consequence that is subsequently measured. Under this proposal, deriving a Page curve inside a model that assumes the relevant duality would be valuable evidence but would not alone complete the innovation.
completion_criteria.label: Independent check beyond Page-curve calculation discriminates between evaporation accounts

completion_criteria.text: Proposed experimental boundary: an acoustic or optical analog reproducing a mode-mixing formula would qualify only if a justified theoretical connection showed that its result discriminates between accounts of gravitational evaporation. A framework's assertion that an analog is relevant would not suffice. The supplied evidence establishes neither such a decisive connection nor an existing feasible observable for an astrophysical test.
completion_criteria.label: Justified gravitational connection makes analog results discriminate between evaporation accounts

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and scope requirements: independent analyses should reproduce the central derivation and assess its sensitivity to initial states, boundary conditions, and approximations. Any physical demonstration should state which systems, observables, and regimes it tests. A finite collection of successful calculations or observations would establish demonstrated breadth within those boundaries, rather than literal universality across all black holes or a complete theory of quantum gravity.
completion_criteria.label: Independent analyses reproduce central derivation and assess its sensitivity

related_concepts.text: Roster comparison: PHY-03, “A laboratory proof that gravity is non-classical,” addresses a different evidential target. PHY-11 asks how information behaves during black-hole evaporation; PHY-03 asks for a laboratory demonstration of non-classical gravity. Both concern the meeting of gravity and quantum physics, but completing either would not automatically complete the other. This distinction is based on the supplied roster title; a detailed PHY-03 record was not provided.

The strongest scientific overlaps are with quantum information and holography. Entanglement wedge reconstruction connects interior observables to information encoded in the radiation or boundary description, while the unitary boundary theory constrains the gravitational account. These tools and frameworks help formulate a resolution, but their use in a particular model does not itself supply independent empirical validation of evaporation.

Roster comparison: PHY-05, “A tested microphysical account of the dark-energy scale,” and PHY-12, “Experimental identification of the physics that sets the Higgs-mass scale,” likewise seek explanatory physics with discriminating evidence. Their targets are different: the dark-energy scale and Higgs-mass scale, respectively, rather than information evolution in black-hole evaporation. A resolution of PHY-11 would not, by itself, settle either scale problem. These are comparisons of the supplied concept titles, without an assertion that the entries share a mechanism.

brief.title: A tested answer to whether black holes erase information
possible: We could know what happens to the information in matter that falls into a black hole as it shrinks away. A tested explanation would establish whether that information survives or whether evaporation breaks quantum physics’ usual rule that information is preserved.
why: Physicists would gain a firm constraint on theories connecting gravity and quantum mechanics. Any successful theory would have to explain how evaporation preserves information, or precisely how and why preservation fails.

sources.showed: In a model representing gravity through a quantum theory on its boundary, Penington derived the expected information-preserving entropy curve and explained how radiation encodes part of the black hole’s interior.
sources.quote:
Directly after the Page time,
interior operators can only be reconstructed from the Hawking radiation if the initial state
of the black hole is known.
sources.cited_for: The work explains how information can escape within a particular theoretical model.
sources.not_established: It does not establish an independently tested explanation of evaporation in real black holes.

sources.who: Ricardo Bulcão Valente Ferrari and Samuel Bueno Soltau
sources.showed: Their preprint survey describes theoretical proposals for preserving information, distinguishes an entropy curve from proof of complete information preservation, and reports a lack of experimental confirmation.
sources.cited_for: The survey explains the remaining theoretical and experimental barriers.
sources.not_established: A survey of proposals does not demonstrate which account of evaporation is physically correct.

shown: Penington’s calculation goes beyond an entropy curve, which tracks quantum correlations during evaporation. It explains how information about the interior can be recovered from radiation in his model. Recovery initially requires knowing the black hole’s starting state; later it works across a wider range of starting states.
missing: A complete explanation must establish the fate of the quantum state throughout evaporation, beyond matching an entropy curve.
An independent test must distinguish competing explanations of what happens to information.
A decisive, feasible measurement of information behavior in real black-hole evaporation remains unidentified.

milestones.label: A framework explains information’s fate throughout evaporation
milestones.explanation: A framework would have to derive the late entropy curve and explain how the quantum state evolves, including any failure to preserve information. Explicit assumptions would let others reproduce and challenge the argument.

milestones.label: An independent check distinguishes competing explanations
milestones.explanation: A separate check would have to discriminate between accounts beyond the calculation producing the entropy curve. Mathematical consistency could validate an explanation conceptually; a measured prediction would test it physically.

milestones.label: A laboratory imitation tests gravitational evaporation
milestones.explanation: A sound or light imitation of a black hole would need a justified connection showing that its result distinguishes accounts of gravitational evaporation. That connection would make the experiment relevant to the paradox.

milestones.label: Independent analyses reproduce the result and establish its scope
milestones.explanation: Independent analyses would have to reproduce the central derivation and test sensitivity to starting states, boundary conditions and approximations. This would establish where the explanation holds.

uncertain: It remains unclear how far the boundary-based model’s conclusions extend to physically relevant black holes.
The radiation expected from astrophysical black holes is extremely weak, leaving the feasibility of a direct test uncertain.
There is no established agreement on what would count as a sufficiently discriminating resolution.

page.title: Resolution of the black-hole information paradox
page.definition: A gravitational account determines quantum-state evolution through black-hole formation and complete evaporation in four spacetime dimensions with asymptotically flat boundary conditions, meaning spacetime approaches flatness far away. Independent analysis establishes whether this evolution is unitary, preserving quantum information, or specifies its failure.

goal.need: In the semiclassical calculation, different pure states of collapsing matter can leave the same mixed radiation after a black hole evaporates. If evaporation is unitary, a distant observer could in principle distinguish what fell in. Genuine information loss would limit what even an observer with complete initial data could predict. The radiation’s entropy alone cannot identify its quantum state. Direct observation is difficult because a solar-mass Schwarzschild black hole has a predicted temperature of 62 nanokelvin against a 2.7 kelvin microwave background.

completion.title: A four-dimensional evaporation map and its information fate are independently verified.
completion.criterion: Derive the complete evolution map for black-hole formation and evaporation in four-dimensional asymptotically flat gravity, including correlations with an external reference system. Determine whether the map is unitary or specifies a nonunitary alternative, and explain why the semiclassical information-loss argument fails or survives. An independent peer-reviewed calculation must reproduce the map and its information fate over the stated initial-state domain. This is theoretical verification; empirical confirmation requires a separate physical test.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback; no common externally adopted completion test was identified.
completion.basis: Searches covered Snowmass TF1 and black-hole white papers, ERC QBH Structure objectives, primary reviews, society and academy criteria, and prize rules. No common acceptance test was found. This fallback combines the published full-state calculation target with independent verification. Four-dimensional asymptotically flat evaporation defines a scope beyond the demonstrated holographic calculation; it does not cover every cosmological setting.

milestones.title: Counting microscopic black-hole states gives ln Ω = A/(4G_D) to leading order.
milestones.criterion: At fixed macroscopic black-hole parameters, count the number Ω of compatible microscopic states. In units ℏ = c = k_B = 1, derive ln Ω = A/(4G_D) to leading order in a regime where the semiclassical area law applies. Here A is the horizon area and G_D is Newton’s constant in D spacetime dimensions.
milestones.set_by: Microstate-counting benchmark used by Strominger and Vafa and recognised in the Snowmass TF1 report; the original demonstration concerns five-dimensional extremal black holes.
milestones.threshold_quote: The Bekenstein-Hawking area-entropy relation $S_{BH}=A/4$ is derived for a class of five-dimensional extremal black holes in string theory

milestones.title: A gravity calculation gives a radiation entropy that rises, turns over and returns to zero.
milestones.criterion: Start with a black hole formed in a pure state and no previously emitted radiation. Calculate the von Neumann entropy of all radiation emitted up to each time during complete evaporation. It must start at zero, rise to a maximum at the Page time, then fall to zero when the hole has disappeared.
milestones.set_by: Page’s pure-state radiation entropy benchmark, applied in gravitational calculations by Penington and discussed in the Snowmass TF1 report.
milestones.threshold_quote: the von Neumann entropy of the Hawking radiation initially increases and then decreases back to zero when the black hole has disappeared.

milestones.title: A k-qubit message is recovered after k+c emitted qubits with mean fidelity at least 1−2^−c.
milestones.criterion: Take a black hole maximally entangled with accessible early radiation. Insert a k-qubit message maximally entangled with an external reference and apply a Haar-random unitary to the hole and message. After k+c new qubits escape, allow a decoder that knows the unitary to act on those qubits and the early radiation. Show that the mean overlap of the decoded message and reference with their original maximally entangled state is at least 1−2^−c, averaged over the unitary.
milestones.set_by: Hayden–Preskill information-recovery benchmark, section 3, equations 6–7; originally formulated for a random-unitary model and subsequently applied by Penington.
milestones.threshold_quote: after averaging over $V^{B}$, the fidelity $F(V^{B})$ deviates from one by no more than $2^{-c}$

milestones.title: Gravity predicts individual matrix elements for black-hole formation and evaporation.
milestones.criterion: For a specified initial state that forms a black hole, calculate individual matrix elements directly from gravitational dynamics. Specify the outgoing radiation states and compute either the transition amplitudes to those states or matrix elements of the outgoing radiation density operator in that basis.
milestones.set_by: Full-state calculation benchmark in Almheiri et al., section 11.2, also identified as an outstanding bulk-calculation problem in the Snowmass TF1 report, section 4.
milestones.threshold_quote: how do we compute individual matrix elements of the S-matrix, or $\rho$, directly from the gravity description (without using a holographic duality)?

milestones.title: A microscopic model reproduces the Hawking emission rate for low-energy scalar particles.
milestones.criterion: For a near-extremal five-dimensional black hole in the dilute-gas regime of the D1–D5 system, calculate the leading emission rate for a neutral, minimally coupled scalar in the spherically symmetric mode. At wavelengths long compared with the black-hole radius, match both the normalization and the frequency dependence of the semiclassical rate at infinity, including the fraction of radiation transmitted through the gravitational potential outside the horizon.
milestones.set_by: Microscopic emission-rate comparison used by Das and Mathur and extended to frequency-dependent greybody factors by Maldacena and Strominger.

not_found: No common completion criterion was found in the programme, society, academy, review or prize-rule searches.
The examined sources do not establish an independently verified complete evolution map for four-dimensional asymptotically flat black-hole evaporation.
No observational protocol with an adopted decision threshold for distinguishing unitary from nonunitary gravitational evaporation was found.
No programme, academy or roadmap statement was found judging the resolution itself unachievable or unworthy of pursuit.
No laboratory measurement was found that tracks quantum information through the complete evaporation of a gravitational black hole.

results.finding: One pure-state AdS collapse model gives a radiation entropy that peaks at the Page time and then falls, with no calculation of its return to zero.
results.detail: The derivation assumes absorbing boundary conditions and uses the quantum Ryu–Takayanagi prescription in the semiclassical regime.
results.quote:
The entanglement entropy therefore peaks at the Page time (deﬁned bySrad = Ahor/4GN)

results.finding: In one AdS evaporation model, a small diary inserted after the Page time is recoverable from the radiation after about one scrambling time.
results.quote:
If the small diary is instead thrown into the black holeafter the Page time, it can

results.finding: For a theoretical class of five-dimensional extremal black holes (no empirical sample), fixed-charge BPS state counting gives ln Ω = A/(4G₅) at leading order.
results.detail: The elliptic genus is a signed count. The authors state that it and the BPS state count have the same leading growth. The supplied arXiv version provides no journal publication or independent replication of the entropy match.

results.detail: The area-law match follows from Eqs. (2.2) and (2.12). A post-publication note flags a concern about non-normalizable fluctuations in the gravitational path integral. The boundary-condition analysis remains open.

results.detail: K is varied in the theoretical calculation. The rank gives a microscopic degeneracy, with the leading term expressed through the extremal entropy parameter S₀.
results.quote:
Thus, as we increase the size of the matrixρmixed BPS above e2Sj its rank saturates,
and all the new states added to the density matrix are linearly dependent on the first
e2Sj states.

results.finding: In one modeled family of evaporating dilaton black holes, the radiation entropy peaks at about one-third of the lifetime.
results.detail: The authors warn that terms dropped in the large-mass limit become significant near the endpoint and that the semiclassical approximation breaks down near the Planck scale.
results.quote: On the left, the Page time for 2D evaporating black holes is approximately one-third of the lifetime.

results.finding: Full Haar ensemble, k-qubit message and k+c emitted qubits: mean optimal recovery fidelity ≥1−2^(−c).
results.detail: The exact expression in Eq. (10) gives d_A d_Bf Δ₂ ≤ 4^(k−r). Substituting it into Theorem 1 yields the finite-size bound. The mean is an analytic Haar integral.
results.quote: \displaystyle\expect_{V^{B}\sim\mu_{\mathbb{U}(d_{B})}}F_{\mathrm{rec}}(V^{B})\gtrsim\frac{1}{1+d_{A}^{2}d_{B_{f}}^{2}/d_{B}^{2}}\gtrsim 1-4^{m-r}\, ,

results.finding: A semiclassical calculation for 2 radiation spin sectors derives amplitude functionals for weak late-time field configurations. No empirical sample applies.
results.detail: Equations (6.19) and (9.18) give the quadratic actions. The late slice is intended to follow emission, but the calculation does not establish complete evaporation for a specified initial state.
results.quote:
The main result is
an explicit expression (6.19) for the classical (linearised) Maxwell ac tion, as a
functional of the ﬁnal magnetic ﬁeld, subject to the simplifying ass umption that
the magnetic ﬁeld on the initial surface Σ I is zero.

results.finding: For one neutral S-wave scalar species, the leading D1–D5 effective-string to greybody-corrected Hawking emission rate ratio is 1.
results.detail: The calculation assumes ωr₅ ≪ 1 and r₀, rₙ ≪ r₁, r₅. It retains the full dependence on ω/TL and ω/TR at leading order.
results.quote:
We see that this exp ression
agrees precisely with (4.35).

results.finding: One five-dimensional D1–D5 model reports semiclassical agreement for minimal-scalar s-wave emission with coupling μ = 1.
results.detail: The coupling is fixed by a two-point function in AdS₃ without a black hole. The supplied text gives no explicit minimal-scalar emission spectrum or transmission factor.
results.quote:
We will see below that the above normalization leads to precise equality between
the absorption cross-sections (and consequently Hawking radiat ion rates) computed from
the moduli space of the D1-D5 system and from semiclassical gravit y.

goal.need = "In the semiclassical calculation, different pure states of collapsing matter can leave the same mixed radiation after a black hole evaporates. If evaporation is unitary, a distant observer could in principle distinguish what fell in. Genuine information loss would limit what even an observer with complete initial data could predict. The radiation\u2019s entropy alone cannot identify its quantum state. Direct observation is difficult because a solar-mass Schwarzschild black hole has a predicted temperature of 62 nanokelvin against a 2.7 kelvin microwave background.". Reason: The temperature comparison explains the obstacle to observation, while the revised text also explains what either outcome would mean for an observer with complete initial data.

add statement by Snowmass Theory Frontier topical group TF1, in its report on quantum gravity, string theory and black holes, 2022: "Extending these results to Schwarzschild black holes remains an important challenge.". Reason: Restoring the subject of the Snowmass statement identifies the specific Schwarzschild microstate problem that the topical group named.

add statement by European Research Council-funded HoloHair project, grant agreement 852386, 2019: "how information is encoded in quantum gravity in asymptotically flat Minkowski spacetime.". Reason: The HoloHair grant explicitly identifies information flow in the asymptotically flat setting specified by the entry.

edit m1: title = "Counting microscopic black-hole states gives ln \u03a9 = A/(4G_D) to leading order."; criterion = "At fixed macroscopic black-hole parameters, count the number \u03a9 of compatible microscopic states. In units \u210f = c = k_B = 1, derive ln \u03a9 = A/(4G_D) to leading order in a regime where the semiclassical area law applies. Here A is the horizon area and G_D is Newton\u2019s constant in D spacetime dimensions.". Reason: The area-law formula states the test, while the five-dimensional example and its submission date describe a particular result.

add milestone after m1: "A microscopic model reproduces the Hawking emission rate for low-energy scalar particles.". Reason: Agreement on the frequency-dependent emission rate tests microscopic dynamics that an equilibrium count of states cannot establish.

edit m2: title = "A gravity calculation gives a radiation entropy that rises, turns over and returns to zero."; criterion = "Start with a black hole formed in a pure state and no previously emitted radiation. Calculate the von Neumann entropy of all radiation emitted up to each time during complete evaporation. It must start at zero, rise to a maximum at the Page time, then fall to zero when the hole has disappeared."; set_by = "Page\u2019s pure-state radiation entropy benchmark, applied in gravitational calculations by Penington and discussed in the Snowmass TF1 report."; threshold_quote = "the von Neumann entropy of the Hawking radiation initially increases and then decreases back to zero when the black hole has disappeared."; threshold_ref = 25; refs = [25, 5, 4, 3]. Reason: Page states the pure-state endpoint explicitly, and the criterion can specify the entire entropy test without embedding Penington’s result or its submission date.

edit m3: criterion = "Take a black hole maximally entangled with accessible early radiation. Insert a k-qubit message maximally entangled with an external reference and apply a Haar-random unitary to the hole and message. After k+c new qubits escape, allow a decoder that knows the unitary to act on those qubits and the early radiation. Show that the mean overlap of the decoded message and reference with their original maximally entangled state is at least 1\u22122^\u2212c, averaged over the unitary."; threshold_quote = "after averaging over $V^{B}$, the fidelity $F(V^{B})$ deviates from one by no more than $2^{-c}$"; threshold_ref = 7. Reason: The fidelity bound requires a maximally entangled message and reference, and the decoder in the proof may depend on the internal unitary.

edit m4: title = "Gravity predicts individual matrix elements for black-hole formation and evaporation."; criterion = "For a specified initial state that forms a black hole, calculate individual matrix elements directly from gravitational dynamics. Specify the outgoing radiation states and compute either the transition amplitudes to those states or matrix elements of the outgoing radiation density operator in that basis."; threshold_quote = "how do we compute individual matrix elements of the S-matrix, or $\\rho$, directly from the gravity description (without using a holographic duality)?"; threshold_ref = 4. Reason: The cited benchmark asks for individual matrix elements in either description, while the current criterion requires the entire density matrix in one of them.

add not found: "No programme, academy or roadmap statement was found judging the resolution itself unachievable or unworthy of pursuit.". Reason: Disagreement over whether evaporation is unitary answers a different question from whether resolving its information fate is worthwhile or achievable.
